Name: Tutor LMS + WooCommerce: intermittent missing (and occasional duplicate) tutor_earnings rows for paid course orders
Details:
Product: Tutor LMS 3.9.9 + Tutor LMS Pro 3.9.9, WooCommerce monetization (monetize_by = wc), HPOS enabled, WooCommerce block/Store-API checkout, Stripe gateway with order auto-complete.
Summary: Tutor inserts duplicate commission rows into {prefix}tutor_earnings for a single order line. The de-duplication guard in Tutor\Classes\WooCommerce::add_earning_data() is a non-atomic SELECT-then-INSERT with no database-level uniqueness, so it loses the race during slow checkouts and writes two identical earnings rows for the same (order_id, course_id, user_id).
Where: tutor/classes/WooCommerce.php, method add_earning_data() (hooked on woocommerce_new_order_item):
$exist_count = (int) $wpdb->get_var( $wpdb->prepare(
"SELECT COUNT(earning_id) FROM {$wpdb->prefix}tutor_earnings
WHERE course_id=%d AND order_id=%d AND user_id=%d",
$course_id, $order_id, $user_id
) );
if ( $exist_count > 0 ) { return; }
// ...
$wpdb->insert( $wpdb->prefix . 'tutor_earnings', $earning_data );
woocommerce_new_order_item can fire more than once for the same line item during a single checkout (Store API re-creates line items when the order/totals are recalculated — e.g. on coupon application, calculate_totals(), or order-from-request updates). Because the existence check and the insert are not atomic and there is no UNIQUE constraint, when two of these fire within one slow checkout request chain (here: Stripe payment-intent → auto-complete → Xero invoice, all synchronous) the second SELECT reads before the first insert's order transaction has committed, returns 0, and a second row is inserted.
Concrete reproduction (production):
Order #17160, course 14298, instructor user 449.
Two identical rows: both order_status = completed, instructor_amount = 32.50, process_by = woocommerce, created 51 seconds apart (19:21:22 and 19:22:13), during a checkout whose Stripe/auto-complete/Xero notes span that exact window.
Net effect: the instructor's native Tutor earnings balance is over-credited by £32.50 (£213.19 vs the correct £180.69). No coupon was on this order — coupon recalculation is one trigger for the duplicate line-item event, but not the only one.
Impact: Instructor earnings and withdrawal totals computed by Tutor (SUM(instructor_amount) over tutor_earnings) are inflated. Frequency is low (race-dependent) but the financial effect is real and silent.
Requested fix: Make the guard atomic. Either (a) add a UNIQUE KEY (order_id, course_id, user_id) to the tutor_earnings schema and use INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY / INSERT IGNORE, or (b) wrap the existence-check + insert in a row/named lock (GET_LOCK) keyed to order_id+course_id+user_id. A DB-level unique constraint is the robust option and is backward-compatible (one earning per order line per instructor; subscription renewals already use distinct order_ids).

Name: Facebook Social Media login does not work.
Details:
While trying to login with Facebook user get email is invalid error and can’t log in.

The root cause is in *addons/social-login/includes/Authentication/Authentication.php line 68*.
The *`verify_facebook_token()`* function calls the Graph API without requesting the email field:
`$response = file_get_contents( "https://graph.facebook.com/me?access_token=$token" );`

It should be:

`$response = file_get_contents( "https://graph.facebook.com/me?fields=id,name,email&access_token=$token" );`

Without fields=email, the verification object has no email to compare against, causing all Facebook logins to fail with “Invalid email”.

Name: Old Failed Stripe Payments Canceling Enrollments
Details:
When a student makes multiple payment attempts for the same course in Stripe:
1. *First attempt fails or is incomplete* → Stripe creates a PaymentIntent.
2. *Second attempt succeeds* → Tutor LMS enrolls the student correctly.
3. *Hours later, Stripe auto-cancels the first failed PaymentIntent* → sends `payment_intent.canceled` webhook.
4. *Tutor LMS handles this webhook* → marks the order as cancelled and *overwrites the existing enrollment* for the course/student.
5. *Result:* Student’s enrollment is cancelled even though a successful payment exists.

Name: Tutor LMS course bundle addon Improvement
Details:
Editing a bundle does not re-enroll existing buyers
When a course inside a bundle is replaced with a different one, students who already purchased the bundle are NOT enrolled in the new course. Their dashboard shows the new course (read from the bundle-course-ids meta) but clicking it returns "no access".
This affected ~150 students on our site and required manual re-enrollment via WP-CLI using tutor_utils()->do_enroll() plus a status change to 'completed' (do_enroll leaves the enrollment as 'pending', which does not grant access — that was another surprise).
Suggested improvement: when a bundle's course list changes, offer to sync enrollments for existing owners, or at least warn the admin that existing buyers will lose access to the removed course and won't gain access to the new one.
FILTER HOOK OBSERVATION
While building a temporary workaround we found what looks like a bug in CourseModel::get_enrolled_courses_by_user() (tutor/models/CourseModel.php, around line 1357):
```$course_args = array(
    'post_type'      => $course_post_type,
    'post_status'    => $post_status,
    'post__in'       => $course_ids,
    'offset'         => $offset,
    'posts_per_page' => $posts_per_page,
    'orderby'        => 'post__in',
);
$args        = apply_filters( 'tutor_get_enrolled_courses_by_user', $args, $user_id, $course_post_type );
$course_args = wp_parse_args( $args, $course_args );```
The filter receives $args — the 5th function parameter, which is an empty array by default — not $course_args, which is the array actually holding post__in with the enrolled IDs. Developers hooking this filter cannot inspect the enrolled course IDs; they have to re-query them with tutor_utils()->get_enrolled_courses_ids_by_user().
Passing $course_args to the filter (or at least including the resolved $course_ids as an extra argument) would make this hook genuinely usable.
CURRENT WORKAROUND
We're filtering tutor_get_enrolled_courses_by_user, tutor_get_active_courses_by_user and tutor_get_completed_courses_by_user to exclude any course ID found in the bundle-course-ids meta of bundles the user owns. It fixes the duplication, but we'd rather rely on native behavior.

Name: Tutor LMS Learning Interface Renders Lesson & Quiz Pages in Quirks Mode (Missing DOCTYPE)
Details:

Name: Assignment Vulnerability
Details:
We have received a confirmed vulnerability report from *Wordfence* regarding a *SQL Injection vulnerability* in *Tutor LMS Pro* plugin. The vulnerability affects the `get_submitted_assignments()` function and was responsibly disclosed to them by a researcher named _sergioframi_.

*Affected Versions*:
• Initially discovered in *v3.6.1*
• Still present in *v3.7.0*
*Vulnerable File & Function*:
• File: `tutor-pro/addons/tutor-assignments/classes/Assignments_List.php`
• Function: `get_submitted_assignments()`
• Line: *419*
*Proof of Concept Payload*:
```       GET /dashboard/assignments/submitted/?assignment=005&order=asc(select*from(select(sleep(20)))a)&current_page=1```
A 20-second delay can be observed, confirming the vulnerability to *time-based blind SQL Injection*.

Wordfence strongly advises using *`$wpdb->prepare()`* for *all dynamic SQL queries* that include user input. Wordfence may notify customers and the public following their coordinated disclosure policy. They request confirmation of receipt *within 14 days* to avoid accelerated disclosure.

Please prioritize this immediately to reduce exposure risk. Let me know if you need anything else from the report.

Name: Gift Course issues
Details:
• Issue: 
    ◦ GiftScheduler.php: comments by sender does not support German "Umlaute" or Emojis ... receiver sees garbage characters instead
    ◦ front.js: Date Formatting causes critical "RangeError" in Safari Browser, with dates like "2025-12-1" - this prohibits completion of Gift-Course Dialog (Button not working)
    ◦ EventHandler.php: DateTime formatting bug, causes problems with tutor_gift_sent_at and tutor_gift_received_at display
    ◦ GiftMailer.php: Email Subject Formatting - {buyer_name} never gets resolved
    ◦ GiftMailer: "Send notification email to the receiver" send-status is not properly updated in database order_itemmeta and related status attributes
Gift Course Patch Summary :

1. UTF‑8 characters in gift notes (GiftScheduler.php)
• *Symptom*: German umlauts and emoji entered by the purchaser arrive as mojibake for the recipient.
• *Root Cause*: `GiftScheduler::schedule()` uses `QueryHelper::insert()`; the helper sanitizes JSON with `Input::sanitize_array()`, which strips UTF‑8 escape sequences.
• *Patch*: Bypass `QueryHelper` and insert via `$wpdb->insert(...)` so the payload JSON is stored untouched.
• *Ask*: Adopt direct `$wpdb` insert (or a UTF‑8 safe helper) so gift messages retain multibyte characters.
2. Safari RangeError in gift dialog (front.js)
• *Symptom*: Safari throws `RangeError: Invalid time value` for dates like `2025-12-1`; the “Proceed to checkout” button never fires.
• *Root Cause*: `new Date("YYYY-M-D HH:mm")` is parsed differently across browsers; Safari rejects single‑digit days.
• *Patch*: Parse date/time manually (`new Date(year, month-1, day, hour, minute)`) before calling `.toISOString()`.
• *Ask*: Replace the string-based constructor with the explicit numeric constructor so Safari users can purchase gifts.
3. Double date formatting in admin (EventHandler.php)
• *Symptom*: `tutor_gift_sent_at` / `tutor_gift_received_at` show “current time” instead of the stored timestamp.
• *Root Cause*: `DateTimeHelper::get_gmt_to_user_timezone_date()` already returns a localized string, but the result is passed again into `tutor_i18n_get_formated_date()`. The second pass runs `strtotime()` on German strings like “1. Dezember…”, which fails and falls back to “now”.
• *Patch*: Use only `DateTimeHelper::get_gmt_to_user_timezone_date()` for display (remove the second formatter).
• *Ask*: Avoid re-formatting localized strings; render the helper’s return value directly.
4. Gift email subject uses nickname (GiftMailer.php)
• *Symptom*: Placeholder `{buyer_name}` resolves to the purchaser’s nickname, not first+last name.
• *Patch*: In `GiftMailer::get_receiver_email_content()`, build `$full_name` from `first_name`/`last_name` (fallback to `display_name`), then replace `{buyer_name}` accordingly.
• *Ask*: Ensure receiver emails always use the real first/last name combination.
5. Generated accounts need first/last name split (GiftEnrollment.php)
• *Symptom*: When the recipient has no account, the auto-created WP user ends up with the entire “Recipient name” field stored as `first_name`.
• *Patch*: Split the form input on whitespace, store the first token as `first_name`, remainder as `last_name`, update `display_name`.
• *Ask*: Apply similar logic when creating guest accounts so WooCommerce mails and certificates show proper names.
6. Gift send status not persisted (GiftMailer.php & GiftScheduler.php)
• *Symptom*: WooCommerce order items remain stuck in `tutor_gift_status=processing`, `tutor_gift_sent_at` stays empty when the cron-based resend executes.
• *Root Causes*:
    a. `GiftMailer::send_notification_email_to_receiver()` didn’t update `GiftCourse::GIFT_STATUS_META` / `GIFT_SENT_AT_META`.
    b. `GiftScheduler::process_scheduled()` instantiated `GiftMailer` without the ecommerce “proceeder”, so the mailer couldn’t call `update_item_meta()` for WooCommerce orders.
• *Patch*:
    ◦ Update status and timestamps inside `send_notification_email_to_receiver()`.
    ◦ Pass the proceeder returned by `GiftCourse::get_gift_proceeder()` into the cron-triggered mailer.
• *Ask*: Ensure both checkout-time and cron-time gift deliveries share the same proceeder so order item meta stays in sync.
These changes keep tutor_gift course purchases functional for German customers and ensure our audit trail (sent timestamps) remains accurate.
